evidence.note: Created a task list where Task 2 explicitly frames work as 'compare main_scores to MTEB leaderboard' — showing awareness that structural passing is not correctness and that numbers must be reconciled to a reference.
Extensive polling of the long retrieval run tracks execution state, but monitoring is coarse (per-type / process-alive) rather than a per-task-of-37 status ledger.
Shared-code edits including a loader fix; downstream types were re-run afterward by sequencing, but no explicit reasoning about re-verifying already-passing tasks affected by the shared change.

Ran full structural validation and printed all main scores, then marked tasks completed — some cross-validation posture, but no visible per-task reconciliation of all 37 against expected values before declaring done.

reasoning: The agent kept a type-level inventory and, via its Task 2 wording and end-of-run printing of all main scores, clearly distinguished 'structurally passing' from 'checked against reference' — matching the level-5 anchor. It did not maintain a fine-grained live ledger across all 37 tasks, nor did it explicitly flag unreconciled tasks or detect shared-code changes silently altering other tasks' numbers (the level-8 behaviors), so it falls at 5 rather than higher.
